findings.title: "Stable recommendation vocabulary" doesn't exist; the routing contract for Amoeba is impossible as specified
findings.description:
The doc says the gate returns `{ recommendation: "review" }` and `{ recommendation: "blocked" }`. Related Work says Amoeba "depends on CF returning structured `recommendation` values with a stable vocabulary — the gate must not change the `NextAction` return type, only add new `recommendation` string values."

That vocabulary doesn't exist. `NextAction.recommendation` (`packages/core/src/introspection/types.ts:281`) is free-form display text. Every existing branch returns prose, such as `` `Continue implementation — ${remaining} tasks remaining` `` and `` `Advance to slice ${nextEntry.index}: ${nextEntry.name}` `` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:240,253`). Two problems follow:
- Adding the bare tokens `"review"` and `"blocked"` mixes machine codes with human sentences in one field.
- No "advance" token exists for a runner to pair them with.

The doc also contradicts itself. Design Goals promises that runners "can act on them without parsing recommendation strings", yet the only channel it gives Amoeba is the recommendation string. `pending-review` and `review-failed` would live on `SliceStatus.status`, which comes from `getStatus()`, not `getNext()`.

The fix needs a decision now, not at slice design. Add a typed discriminator, such as `action: 'review' | 'blocked' | 'advance' | ...` as an `as const` union, to `NextAction`. That is an additive, optional field, so it doesn't break the type. Then drop the claim that `recommendation` is a stable vocabulary. The project rule is "NEVER use user-accessible labels as logical structure", and the current design does exactly that.

findings.title: Three of the four "v1 slice-level transitions" have no insertion point in the design
findings.description:
Initiative-level gating says "V1 implements only the four slice-level transitions." But the config sample has only three slice-level gates (`pre-tasks`, `pre-implementation`, `pre-advance`); the fourth, `pre-slice-plan`, is the deferred initiative gate.

Of those three, the design only covers `pre-advance`:
- There is one new branch, between Priority 5 and Priority 6.
- `pending-review` is defined as "tasks complete … no review artifact present".
- The anticipated "Gate logic" slice only extends the `complete` path.

`pre-tasks` would need to block between `needs-tasks` and task-file creation (Priority 4). `pre-implementation` would need to block between task-file creation and `in-implementation` (Priority 5). Neither has a status value, an insertion point or a rationale string.

`pre-implementation` also has an unaddressed semantic problem. `deriveSliceStatus()` only infers `in-implementation` from checkbox state. Once one box is checked, the navigator can't tell "implementation started without a tasks review" from "tasks review passed". The gate would have to override in-progress status, and that conflicts with "`review-failed` is distinct from `in-progress`."

Either scope v1 to `pre-advance` only (recommended; see the proportionality finding below) or specify all three gates.

findings.title: Saying "both surfaces inherit it with no per-surface work" is false: WorkflowNavigator has no config access
findings.description:
`WorkflowNavigator` is stateless and built with no arguments at four call sites:
- `packages/cli/src/commands/next.ts:26`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:119`
- `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts:154,200`

`getNext(project)` takes only `ProjectData`. Config is resolved at the surface layer today; `workflow.auto_fix` is read via `cm.get(...)` in `check.ts:141` and `workflowTools.ts:263`.

The gate needs `review_enabled`, `review_threshold`, `review_unknown_as`, `review_gates` and the worktree-scoped resolution from 180. So either every surface resolves and passes a review policy (per-surface work, which the doc denies), or the navigator takes on a config-manager dependency.

The doc picks neither. Recommendation: inject a resolved `ReviewPolicy` value object through the `WorkflowNavigator` and `ConsistencyChecker` constructors, built by one shared factory that applies 180's resolution chain. Then state that in the architecture.

findings.title: The current frontmatter parser can't do what the verdict-reading design needs
findings.description:
`parseFrontmatter()` (`parsers/frontmatterParser.ts`) is a flat line-by-line `key: value` splitter. It returns `Record<string, string>` and "Never throws — returns `{ found: false, data: {} }` on any error". That clashes with the design in three ways:
- **Errors are swallowed.** File-read failure modes says "the rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly." This parser makes permission errors, malformed YAML, a missing closing `---` and "no frontmatter" indistinguishable.
- **No opaque carrying.** Architectural Principles says CF "carries `criteria` and `provenance` as opaque fields." If either is a YAML map or list, as provenance and criteria almost certainly are, nested lines become bogus top-level keys and can even overwrite real ones (a nested `verdict:` under `criteria` would clobber the top-level verdict).
- **No float.** `score` ("float 0–100") arrives as a string.

The doc needs to say whether review frontmatter gets a real YAML parser (the stack's `yaml` package or similar) returning a `Result` type. As written, the "artifact-first truth" principle rests on a parser that can't report what it saw.

findings.title: The existing catch-all in `deriveSliceStatus()` would silently defeat the fail-closed gate
findings.description:
`deriveSliceStatus()` wraps all detection in `try { … } catch { return base; }`, where `base.status = 'no-active-slice'` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:462–496`). If review discovery or verdict reading is added inside that block, as "Extend `deriveSliceStatus()`" implies, any exception sends the project to Priority 2 ("pick your first slice"). It won't land in `review-failed` or `UNKNOWN`, and nothing gets logged. The gate fails open, the opposite of the conservative-default principle.

Separately, `SliceStatus` carries only `status` and `taskProgress`. It has no slot for the verdict, the matched file, the threshold or a parse-error reason. So `getNext()` can't produce the rationale strings shown ("verdict FAIL does not clear threshold 'concerns'", "names the parse failure explicitly") without extending `SliceStatus`.

The design needs to:
- Specify a `review?: { file: string | null; verdict: Verdict; threshold: Threshold; reason?: string }` field.
- Require review evaluation to sit outside the swallow-all catch, or that catch to be narrowed.

findings.title: Verdict, threshold and unknown-policy vocabularies are inconsistent and not enumerated
findings.description:
- Verdicts are uppercase (`PASS`, `CONCERNS`), while threshold values are lowercase (`"concerns"`, `"pass"`). The case-mapping rule is never stated.
- Technical Considerations uses `review_unknown_as = "concern"` (singular). Every other place uses `concerns`.
- The Slice status extension section implies a third `review_unknown_as` value ("verdict is `UNKNOWN` and `review_unknown_as` treats it as pending"). The allowed values (`fail` | `concerns` | `pending`?) are never listed, so the fail-fast `validate` hook has nothing to validate against.
- "CONCERNS — clears if threshold = concerns **or lower**": no ordering of thresholds below `concerns` is defined. With `PASS` always clearing and `FAIL` always blocking, the only meaningful values are `pass` and `concerns`. Say so.
- Which status `UNKNOWN` maps to under `fail` (`review-failed` or `pending-review`) is never said.

Define each vocabulary once as an `as const` union in core (per project rule "define it once") and list the allowed values in the doc.

findings.title: The `review_gates` config schema is a load-bearing decision that was deferred
findings.description:
`ConfigKeyDefinition` (`config/ConfigKeys.ts:1–7`) only models scalar `string | boolean | number` keys with an optional `enum` and `validate`. Per-transition overrides are central to the "config-driven" goal and to the fail-fast principle ("an unrecognized per-gate config is a config error"). Yet the schema is left as "a decision is needed at slice design time".

Both options affect the 180 worktree resolution chain and the `cf config get/set` surface:
- **Nested tables** need a new shape type plus merge semantics across scopes.
- **Flat dotted keys** need a key-pattern registry, because `workflow.review_gates.pre-advance.reviewType` can't be a static entry in `CONFIG_KEYS` without enumerating every combination.

Yet the first anticipated slice is told to "add … per-gate override structure to `ConfigKeys.ts`." Decide here. If v1 is scoped to `pre-advance` only, the nested-table problem goes away entirely; see the proportionality finding below.

findings.title: Choosing the lexicographically last file is not "most recent", and the discovery convention isn't pinned down
findings.description:
The pattern is `NNN-review.{reviewType}.*.md`, where `*` is a descriptive slug (for example `github-copilot-vs-code-ide-support`). Two `code` reviews for one index differ only in slug, and slug sort order has nothing to do with time. `…code.zz-old.md` beats `…code.aa-rerun.md`. Calling this "most recent by sort order" is wrong, and it can resurrect a stale `FAIL` over a newer `PASS`, or the reverse.

There are three ways to fix it:
- Require a sortable round or date token in the filename.
- Read a frontmatter date (`dateCreated` or a provenance timestamp).
- Treat multiple matches as a `warning` finding.

The doc also doesn't say:
- Whether `reviews/` is resolved through the existing artifact-path resolution or hard-coded.
- Whether the arch review index is the arch's index or the slice's index.
- That `ProjectModelBuilder.ts:483` already classifies `docType === 'review'` documents. Discovery should reuse that rather than add a second filename matcher, per DRY.

findings.title: The ConsistencyChecker rule will flag every historical slice as soon as gating is enabled
findings.description:
The rule fires on any slice "marked complete in the slice plan" without a required review. A mature project that turns on `review_enabled = true` will get a warning for every slice completed before review artifacts existed. `cf check` becomes noise, and the actionable findings for the active slice are buried.

The design needs a scope, for example:
- only the active slice,
- only slices completed after a configured baseline,
- or a `workflow.review_since` key.

Also, the checker emits `error` for a failing verdict while the navigator treats the same state as a routing position (`blocked`). Say whether `cf check` exiting non-zero on a routine `review-failed` state is intended for CI users.

findings.title: The design is heavier than v1 needs: cut it to a single `pre-advance` gate
findings.description:
The stated problem (Motivation, Current State) is one missing node between "tasks complete" and "advance". The design builds much more:
- three global keys,
- a four-entry per-transition override table with `reviewType` remapping,
- an unknown-verdict policy that interacts with threshold (which Technical Considerations itself warns "must be documented clearly to avoid support confusion"),
- a "documented code path" for score enforcement that nothing uses,
- a defined but unimplemented `pre-slice-plan` transition.

What to cut or defer:
- the `review_gates` table (v1: a single `pre-advance` gate with `reviewType = code` implied);
- `pre-tasks` and `pre-implementation` (no insertion points exist anyway; see the second FAIL finding);
- the score-enforcement code path (add it when Squadron 301 ships);
- `review_unknown_as` (fold `UNKNOWN` into fail-closed, which is already the default).

That leaves `review_enabled` and `review_threshold`. It also removes the deferred config-schema decision and the nested-TOML problem.

findings.title: Smaller inconsistencies with the code
findings.description:
- `SliceStatus` is an interface with a `status` string-literal union (`types.ts:254–263`), not an enum. The values go into that union.
- "`review-failed` is distinct from `in-progress`": the slice status is `in-implementation`. `in-progress` is the task-file `inferredStatus`.
- `workflow.auto_advance` is defined in `ConfigKeys.ts` but nothing reads it. The `auto_advance` interaction section reasons about a consumer that doesn't exist; harmless, but don't count it as validated.
- Adding union members affects `buildSummary()` and the CLI/MCP status tests (`status.test.ts`, `workflowTools.test.ts`, `worktree-overlay.test.ts`). The anticipated slices should list those surfaces, and the visualizer that Design Goals mentions.
- Renumbering the `getNext()` cascade is assigned to the "discovery and config keys" slice, which adds no branch. It belongs with the gate-logic slice that actually inserts the new priority.
- `riskLevel: low` understates a change to the core status union and the navigator's routing contract, which external runners consume.
